label: defco
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defco}
Given a sequence $v_k$ with  $v_k\in H^1((a,b);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ and $v\in H^1((a,b);\mathbb R^d)$ we write $v_k\to v$ if 
for all subsequences $v_{k_j}$, there exist a subsequence, which we still denote by $v_{k_j}$, 
and $\widehat v\in H^1((a,b);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$, possibly depending on the subsequence, such that 
$$
 v_{k_j}\rightharpoonup \widehat v \hbox{ weakly in }H^1((a,b);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)),
\qquad
\mathbb E(\widehat v(t))=v(t)\hbox{ for every }t.
$$
head: environment
name: convergence to a deterministic variable

label: main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main} Let $F_\varepsilon$ be given by \eqref{deffe}. Given $\varepsilon_k\to 0$, we have

\smallskip
{\rm(i)} For every $v\in H^1(a,b)$ and for every sequences $\mathcal F^k_t$,  $B^k_t$, and $v_k\to v$ such that 
$v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable, we have 
$$
F_{\rm hom} (v)\le\liminf_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t);
$$

\smallskip
{\rm(ii)} for every $v\in H^1(a,b)$ there exists sequences  $\mathcal F^k_t$,  $B^k_t$, and $v_k\to v$, such that 
$v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable,  such that
$$
F_{\rm hom} (v)\ge\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t).
$$
head: environment

label: lemmada
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmada} Let $V_k\colon(0,1)\times \mathbb R^d\to \mathbb R$ be Borel functions such that there exists $M>0$ with $|V_k(t,x)|\le M$ for all $k\in\mathbb N$, $t\in(0,1)$, and $x\in\mathbb R^d$. We define
\begin{equation}\label{degde}
G_k(z)=\int_0^1\mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot z(t)|^2dt+V_k(t,z(t))\Big)dt
\end{equation}
for $z
\in H^1((0,1),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$.
Let $\mathcal G^k_t$ be a sequence of filtrations and let $z_k\in H^1((0,1),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$
be such that $z_k(t)$ is  $\mathcal G^k_t$-measurable for every $t\in(0,1)$. Assume that $z_k\rightharpoonup \widehat z$ weakly in $H^1((0,1),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$.
Then, given $\eta>0$ there exists a sequence $\widetilde z_k$ in $H^1((0,1),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ such that 

\smallskip
{\rm (i)} $\widetilde z_k\rightharpoonup \widehat z$ weakly in $H^1((0,1),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$;

\smallskip
{\rm (ii)} $\widetilde z_k(t)$ is  $\mathcal G^k_t$-measurable for every $t\in(0,1)$; 

\smallskip
{\rm (iii)} $G_{k} (\widetilde z_k) \le G_{k} (z_k)+\eta$ for $k$ large enough;

\smallskip
{\rm (iv)} $\mathbb E(\widetilde z_k(0))=\mathbb E(\widehat z(0))$ and $\mathbb E(\widetilde z_k(1))=\mathbb E(\widehat z(1))$.
head: environment
name: variation of boundary data

title: Proof
body_md:
We first note that $\mathbb E(z_k(0))\to\mathbb E(\widehat z(0))$ (and similarly $\mathbb E(z_k(1))\to\mathbb E(\widehat z(1))$).
We set $\alpha_k=\mathbb E(z_k(0))-\mathbb E(\widehat z(0))$ and $\beta_k=\mathbb E(z_k(1))-\mathbb E(\widehat z(1))$. Let $\delta>0$ and let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ with $0\le\varphi\le 1$ and $\varphi=1$ in $(\delta,1-\delta)$. We set
$$
\widetilde z_k(t)=\begin{cases} z_k(t)-(1-\varphi(t))\alpha_k & \hbox{ if } t\in(0,\delta)\\
 z_k(t) &\hbox{ if } t\in[\delta,1-\delta]\\
z_k(t)-(1-\varphi(t))\beta_k & \hbox{ if } t\in(1-\delta,1),
 \end{cases}
$$
so that
$$
\dot{\widetilde z}_k(t)=\begin{cases} \dot z_k(t) +\dot \varphi(t)\alpha_k & \hbox{ if } t\in(0,\delta)\\
\dot z_k(t) &\hbox{ if } t\in[\delta,1-\delta]\\
\dot z_k(t) +\dot \varphi(t)\beta_k & \hbox{ if } t\in(1-\delta,1)
 \end{cases}
$$
Properties (ii) and (iv) are true by construction, and (i) follows since  $\alpha_k,\beta_k\to 0$.
To prove (iii) we compute 
\begin{eqnarray*}
G_k (\widetilde z_k)&=& \int_0^{1} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot{\widetilde z}_k(t)|^2+ V_k(t, \widetilde z_k(t))\Big)dt
\\
&\le& \int_{\delta}^{1-\delta} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot{z}_k(t)|^2+  V_k(t, z_k(t))\Big)dt
\\
&&
+\int_0^{\delta} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot{z}_k(t)|^2+ \alpha_k\dot{z}_k(t)\dot \varphi(t) +\frac12\alpha_k^2 |\dot{\varphi}(t)|^2\Big)dt
\\
&&
+\int_{1-\delta}^1 \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot{z}_k(t)|^2+ \beta_k\dot{z}_k(t)\dot \varphi(t) +\frac12\beta_k^2 |\dot{\varphi}(t)|^2\Big)dt
+2\delta \max |V_k|
\\
&\le& G_k(z_k)
+\int_0^{\delta} \mathbb E\Big(\alpha_k\dot{z}_k(t)\dot \varphi(t) +\frac12\alpha_k^2 |\dot{\varphi}(t)|^2\Big)dt
\\
&&
+\int_{1-\delta}^1 \mathbb E\Big(\beta_k\dot{z}_k(t)\dot \varphi(t) +\frac12\beta_k^2 |\dot{\varphi}(t)|^2\Big)dt
+4\delta M.
\end{eqnarray*}
Since $\alpha_k$ and $\beta_k\to 0$, claim (iii) follows by the arbitrariness of $\delta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We will use the blow-up method \cite{FM,BMS}, applied to the measures $\mu_k=g_k\mathcal L$, where
$$
g_k(t)=\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v_{k}(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big) .
$$
It is not restrictive to suppose that there exists the limit
$$
\lim_{k\to+\infty}\mu_k((a,b))=\lim_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)<+\infty.
$$
Hence, we can suppose that $\mu_k$ converge weakly* to  a bounded Radon measure $\mu$ on $(a,b)$. We let $\frac{d \mu}{dt}$ denote the density of its absolutely continuous part with respect to the Lebesgue measure $\mathcal L$.


We fix $t_0\in(a,b)$ a Lebesgue point for $\dot v$ such that
$$
\frac{d \mu}{dt}(t_0)=\lim_{\rho\to 0}\frac1{\rho}\mu((t_0,t_0+\rho)),
$$
and note that $\mathcal L$-almost every $t_0\in(a,b)$ satisfies this property. Since $\mu_k((t_0,t_0+\rho))\to \mu((t_0,t_0+\rho))$ except for at most a countable set of $\rho$, we can find $\rho_k\to 0$ such that
$$
\frac{d \mu}{dt}(t_0)= \lim_{k\to +\infty}\frac1{\rho_k}\mu_k((t_0,t_0+\rho_k));
$$
that is, 
\begin{equation}\label{limmu}
\frac{d \mu}{dt}(t_0)= \lim_{k\to +\infty}
\frac1{\rho_k}\int_{t_0}^{t_0+\rho_k}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v_{k}(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big)dt.
\end{equation}

With $\widehat v$ as in Definition \ref{defco}, we can also assume that $t_0$ is such that $(\widehat v(t_0+\rho)- \widehat v(t_0))/\rho$ converges strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $\rho\to 0^+$ to $\widehat \xi\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, the derivative of $\widehat v$ in $t_0$. We can then assume in addition that the parameter $\rho_k>0$ is also such that the scaled functions $z_k(t)=\frac1{\rho_k}(v_k(t_0+\rho_k t)- v_k(t_0))$ converge strongly  in $L^2((0,1),L^2(\Omega);\mathbb R^d)$ to $\widehat z(t)=\widehat \xi t$. 

In order to apply  Lemma \ref{lemmada} we now write
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\hskip-.5cm\frac1{\rho_k}\int_{t_0}^{t_0+\rho_k}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v_{k}(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big)dt
\\
&&=\int_{0}^{1}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v_{k}(t_0+\rho_kt)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_{t_0+\rho_k t}+ v_k(t_0+\rho_k t)}{\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big)dt
\\
&&=\int_{0}^{1}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot z_{k}(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_{t_0+\rho_k t}+v_k(t_0)+\rho_ k z_k(t)} {\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big)dt
\\
&&=\int_{0}^{1}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot z_{k}(t)|^2+ V_k (t,z_k(t))\Big)dt,
\end{eqnarray*}
where 
$$
V_k(t,x)= V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_{t_0+\rho_k t}+v_k(t_0)+\rho_ k x }
{\varepsilon_k}\Big).
$$

By applying Lemma \ref{lemmada} with the filtration $\mathcal G^k_t:=\mathcal F^k_{t_0+\rho_k t}$, we obtain $\widetilde z_k$ satisfying claims (i)--(iv) of that lemma, with $\widehat z(t)= \widehat \xi t$. As a consequence, by \eqref{limmu} we have
$$
\liminf_{k\to+\infty} \int_{0}^{1}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot z_{k}(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_{t_0+\rho_k t}+v_k(t_0)+\rho_ k \widetilde z_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}\Big)\Big)dt\le \frac{d \mu}{dt}(t_0)+\eta.
$$


Changing variables 
$$
s=\frac{\rho_k}{\varepsilon_k}t,\qquad T_k= \frac{\rho_k}{\varepsilon_k},\qquad w_k(s)=\frac{\rho_k}{\varepsilon_k}\, \widetilde z_k\Big(\frac{\varepsilon_k}{\rho_k} s\Big) +\frac{v_k(t_0)}{\varepsilon_k},
$$
we can rewrite the integral as 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{limTk}\nonumber
&&\frac1{T_k}\int_{0}^{T_k}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot w_{k}(s)|^2+ V_{\rm per} 
\Big(\frac{B^k_{t_0+\varepsilon_k s}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}}+ w_k(s)\Big)\Big)ds.
\\
&&=\frac1{T_k}\int_{0}^{T_k}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot w_{k}(s)|^2+ V_{\rm per} 
\Big(\frac{B^k_{t_0+\varepsilon_k s}-{B^k_{t_0}}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}}+ \frac{{B^k_{t_0}}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}}+ w_k(s)\Big)\Big)ds.
\end{eqnarray}


We then define 
$$
\widehat w_k(s):=w_k(s){+\frac{B^k_{t_0}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}}},\qquad\qquad
\widehat B^k_s:=\frac{B^k_{t_0+\varepsilon_k s}- B^k_{t_0}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}},
$$
 and  rewrite \eqref{limTk} as 
\begin{equation}\label{limTk1}
\frac1{T_k}\int_{0}^{T_k}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12{ \big|\dot{\widehat w}_{k}(s)\big|^2}+ V_{\rm per} 
({\widehat B^k_s}+ 
\widehat w_k(s))\Big)ds.
\end{equation}
If we define the filtration $\widehat {\mathcal F}^k_s:= \mathcal F^k_{t_0+\varepsilon_k s}$, to which the Brownian motion  $\widehat B^k_s$ is adapted, then $(\widehat {\mathcal F}^k_s,\widehat B^k_s,\widehat w_k)$ is a test triplet for the problem in \eqref{fomd} for $T=T_k$, since $\mathbb E(\widehat w_k(T_k))-\mathbb E(\widehat w_k(0))=\mathbb E(w_k(T_k)-w_k(0))= \mathbb E(\widehat\xi) T_k= \dot v(t_0)T_k$.
We then obtain 
$$
\frac{d \mu}{dt}(t_0)+\eta\ge f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t_0)),
$$
which then holds for $\mathcal L$-almost all $t_0\in(a,b)$, and finally,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\lim_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)
&=&\lim_{k\to+\infty}\mu_k(a,b)\ge \mu(a,b)\\
&\ge& \int_a^b\frac{d \mu}{dt}(t)dt\ge \int_a^b f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t))dt-\eta(b-a),
\end{eqnarray*}
which gives the lower bound by the arbitrariness of $\eta>0$.
head: environment

label: correct
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{correct}
With fixed $\xi\in\mathbb R^d$,  $\eta>0$, $K>0$, $T_0>0$ there exist $T>T_0$, $r>0$, a filtration $\mathcal F^\xi_t$, a function $w^\xi \in H^1((0,R),L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for all $R>0$, and a Brownian motion $B^\xi_t$, with both $w^\xi$ and $B^\xi_t$ adapted to $\mathcal F^\xi_t$,  such that for all $0\le s_1<s_2<+\infty$
\begin{eqnarray}\label{tre-b}\nonumber
&&\mathbb E\Big(\int_{s_1}^{s_2} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}{}^\xi(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^\xi_t+ w^\xi(t))\Big)dt\Big)
\\
&\le&{
(s_2-s_1)\Big( f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta +\big(3\frac{K}T+{2}\eta_K\big)\max|V_{\rm per}|\Big)}+ C(\xi, T, K, \eta),
\end{eqnarray}
where
$$
C(\xi,T,K,\eta):=
2T (f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta) +2(4K+T(1+{2}\eta_K))\max|V_{\rm per}|\Big),\\
$$
and $\eta_K\to 0$ as $K\to+\infty$. Moreover, for all $j\in\mathbb N$, we have
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E(w^\xi(jT+(j-1)K)) -\mathbb E(w^\xi(0))= jT\xi .
\end{equation}
head: environment

label: mineta
title: Proof
body_md:
We choose $T>T_0$ such that 
$$
\frac1T\min\bigg\{\int_0^T \mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B_t+ w(t))\Big)dt:\mathcal F_t, w\in X_0^T(\xi), B_t\bigg\}<  f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\frac\eta2.
$$
Recall that $X_0^T(\xi)$ depends on the filtration $\mathcal F_t$. 
Therefore, there exist a filtration $\mathcal F_t$, a function $w\in X_0^T(\xi)$, and a Brownian motion $B_t$ adapted to $\mathcal F_t$, such that 
\begin{equation}\label{mineta}
\frac1T \int_0^T \mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B_t+ w(t))\Big)dt< f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\frac\eta2.
\end{equation}
The function $w$ is extended as a constant $w(t)(\omega)=w(T)(\omega)$ for $t>T$. 

In order to proceed inductively in the following, we will need independent copies of $B_t$ and $w$.
To that end, we note that, up to enlarging $\Omega$, we can find a sequence of mutually independent filtrations $\mathcal F^j_t$, a sequence of Brownian motions $B^j_t$, adapted to $\mathcal F^j_t$, and corresponding $w^j$ defined on the same $(0,T)$ belonging to the corresponding $X_0^{j,T}(\xi)$, equivalent to $B_t$ and $w$; that is, such that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{equibw}
&\displaystyle \int_0^T \mathbb E\big(|\dot w^j(t)|^2\big)dt=
\int_0^T \mathbb E\big(|\dot w(t)|^2\big)dt,&
\\ \label{equibw-2}
 &\displaystyle \int_0^T \mathbb E\big(V_{\rm per}(B^j_t+ w^j(t))\big)dt
= \int_0^T \mathbb E\big(V_{\rm per}(B_t+ w(t))\big)dt.&
\end{eqnarray}
Indeed, we can replace $\Omega$ with $\Omega^\mathbb N$ with the product probability. After denoting $\pi_j$ the projection on the $j$-th factor, we define the filtrations 
$$
\mathcal F^j_t=\{ \pi_j^{-1}(A): A\in \mathcal F_t\}.
$$
Note that, given distinct indices $j_1,\ldots, j_m\in\mathbb N$, arbitrary times  $t_1,\ldots, t_m\in[0,T]$, and  a family $E_i\in \mathcal F^{j_i}_{t_i}$ we have
$$
P(E_1\cap\ldots\cap E_m)=\prod_{i=1}^mP(E_i);
$$
that is, $\mathcal F^j_t$ are independent. We then set
$$
B^j_t=B_t \circ \pi_j,\qquad w^j(t)=w(t)\circ \pi_j,
$$
both of which are adapted to $\mathcal F^j_t$. 
Note that \begin{equation}\label{cowj}
w^j(t)=w^j(T)\hbox{ for all $j$ and for all $t>T$}.
\end{equation}
Note that for almost every $t\ge 0$ the laws of $\dot w^j(t)$ and $B^j_t+w^j(t)$ coincide with the corresponding laws of $\dot w(t)$ and $B_t+w(t)$, from which we obtain
equalities \eqref{equibw} and \eqref{equibw-2}.

For all $j\in\mathbb N\cup\infty$ we also introduce the filtration
$$
\widetilde{\mathcal F}^j_t:=\sigma\Big(\bigcup_{i=1}^j\mathcal F^i_t\Big).
$$

\smallskip
To define $B^\xi_t$ and $w^\xi$ on the half line $(0,+\infty)$ we proceed by defining inductively Brownian motions $\widetilde B^j_t$ and functions $\widetilde w_j$, and then setting $B^\xi_t=\widetilde B^j_t$ and $w^\xi=\widetilde w_j$ on intervals $(\tau^\xi_{j-1},\tau^\xi_{j})$ between two suitable stopping times. 


Let $\widetilde \tau_0=0$. We fix $r>0$ such that the modulus of continuity $\lambda$ for $V_{\rm per}$ satisfies $\lambda(r)<\eta/2$.
We consider the {\em stopping time} $\tau_1$ with respect to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^2_t$ defined as the minimal $t\ge T$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{r-1}
{\rm dist}(B^1_t+w^1(T)-w^2(0),\mathbb Z^d)\le r.
\end{equation}
Note that in the scalar case $d=1$ this stopping time can be replaced by the one defined by the condition
\begin{equation}\label{simpz-1}
B^1_t+w^1(T)-w^2(0)\in\mathbb Z,
\end{equation}
avoiding the error term $r$. The same remark holds for the stopping times $\tau_j$ defined in the following.

For fixed $K>0$ there exits $\eta_K>0$, with $\eta_K\to 0$ as $K\to+\infty$, such that, having set $\Omega^1_K=\{\tau_1>T+ K\}$, we have  $P(\Omega^1_K)<\eta_K$  {(see Proposition \ref{apbrown})}. In other words we have $\tau_1\le T+ K$ on $\Omega\setminus\Omega^1_K$.

Let $\widetilde \tau_1=\tau_1\wedge (T+K)$, so that $T\le \widetilde \tau_1\le T+K$.
We set 
$$
 \widetilde B^1_t=B^1_t,\qquad\widetilde w^1(t) =w^1(t),
$$
recalling that $w^1(t)=w^1(T)$ for $t\ge T$, so that 
\begin{equation}\mathbb E(\widetilde w^1(T))=\xi T+ \mathbb E(w^1(0)).
\end{equation} 
Note that
$$
\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^1_t+ {\widetilde w}^1(t))\Big)dt
=\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^1_t+ {w}^1(t))\Big)dt
$$
$$
=\int_0^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^1_t+ {w}^1(t))\Big)dt
+\int_T^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^1_t+ {w}^1(t))\Big)dt
$$
Hence, by \eqref{mineta},  \eqref{equibw} and \eqref{cowj}, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\hskip-1cm\mathbb E\Big(\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^1_t+ {\widetilde w}^1(t))\Big)dt\Big)
\\
&&= \int_0^T \mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B_t+ w(t))\Big)dt
+\mathbb E
\Big(\int_T^{\widetilde \tau_1} V_{\rm per}(B^1_t+ {w}^1(T))dt
\Big)
\\
&&\le \int_0^T \mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B_t+ w(t))\Big)dt
+\mathbb E
\Big(\int_T^{\widetilde \tau_1} |V_{\rm per}(B^1_t+ {w}^1(T))|dt
\Big)
\\
&&\le 
T\Big( f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\frac\eta2\Big) +K\max V_{\rm per}.
\end{eqnarray*}


\smallskip
In order to illustrate the induction argument we preliminarily deal with $j=2$. We define $\widetilde w^2(t)$ and $\widetilde B^2_t$ as follows. We set 
$$
\widetilde w^2(t)=  \begin{cases}\widetilde w^1(t) &\hbox{ for } 0\le t\le \widetilde \tau_{1}\\
\widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t-\widetilde\tau_{1})-  w^2(0)
&\hbox{ for }t> \widetilde \tau_{1}.\end{cases}
$$
Observe that $\widetilde w^2\in H^1((0,R);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for every $R>0$, and that for every $t>0$ the function $w^2(t)$ is $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^2_t$-measurable. Note moreover that, since $\widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})=w^1(T)$, 
 \begin{equation}
 \widetilde w^2(t)=\widetilde w^2(T+\widetilde\tau_{1})=
w^1(T)+ w^2(T)-  w^2(0)\quad\hbox{ if }t\ge T+\widetilde\tau_{1};
 \end{equation}
in particular, 
 \begin{equation}
 \widetilde w^2(t)=\widetilde w^2(2T+K)=w^1(T)+ w^2(T)-  w^2(0)\quad\hbox{ if }t\ge 2T+K
 \end{equation}
 since 
 $\widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})=w^1(T)$ and $w^2(2T+K-\widetilde\tau_{1})=w^2(T)$, recalling that $2T+K-\widetilde\tau_{1} \ge T$.
 
We also set
$$
\widetilde B^2_t = \begin{cases}\widetilde B^1_t  &\hbox{ for } 0\le t\le \widetilde \tau_{1} \\
 B^2_{t-\widetilde \tau_{1} } + \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1} }  &\hbox{ for }t> \widetilde \tau_{1} .\end{cases}
$$
By the strong Markov property this formula defines a Brownian motion on $[0,+\infty)$ adapted to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^2_t$ (see Proposition \ref{concat}). This argument will be used iteratively in the following.


We define the stopping time $\tau_{2} $ with respect to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^3_t$  as the minimal $t\ge 2T+K$ such that
$$
{\rm dist}(\widetilde B^2_t  + \widetilde w^2(t) - w^3(0) ,\mathbb Z^d)\le r,
$$
or, equivalently, such that
$$
{\rm dist}(\widetilde B^2_t  + \widetilde w^2(\widetilde\tau_{1} +T) - w^3(0) ,\mathbb Z^d)\le r,
$$
recalling that $w^2(t)=w^2(T)$ for $t\ge T$.
We then set $\widetilde\tau_{2} = \tau_{2} \wedge( 2T+ 2K),
$
so that $2T+K\le \widetilde \tau_2\le 2T+2K$.
Note that, having set $\Omega^2_K=\{\widetilde\tau_{2}\neq \tau_{2}\}$, we still have $P(\Omega^2_K)\le\eta_K$. 

Using the definitions of $\widetilde B^2_t$ and ${\widetilde w}^2$ we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_2} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))\Big)dt
\\&&
=\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))\Big)dt +
\int_{\widetilde \tau_1}^{\widetilde \tau_2} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))\Big)dt
\\
&&
=\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^1_t+ {\widetilde w}^1(t))\Big)dt 
\\
&&\quad+
\int_{\widetilde \tau_1}^{\widetilde \tau_1+T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t-\widetilde \tau_1)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t-\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t-\widetilde\tau_{1})-  w^2(0))\Big)dt
\\
&&\quad
+\int_{\widetilde \tau_1+T}^{\widetilde \tau_2} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))\Big)dt
\\
&&
=\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_1} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^1(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^1_t+ {\widetilde w}^1(t))\Big)dt 
\\
&&\quad
+
\int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+ \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t)-  w^2(0))\Big)dt
\\
&&\quad
+\int_{\widetilde \tau_1+T}^{\widetilde \tau_2} V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))dt.
\end{eqnarray*}

On $\Omega\setminus\Omega^1_K$ we then have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+ \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t)-  w^2(0))\Big)dt
\\
\le \int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+w^2(t))\Big)dt +\lambda(r) T.
\end{eqnarray*}
Note that in dimension $1$ we can omit this error term.

On $\Omega^1_K$
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&
\int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+ \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t)-  w^2(0))\Big)dt
\\&&=
\int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+w^2(t))\Big)dt\\
&&\quad+\int_{0}^{T} \Big(V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+ \widetilde B^1_{\widetilde \tau_{1}}+ \widetilde w^1(\widetilde\tau_{1})+ w^2(t)-  w^2(0))-V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+w^2(t))\Big)dt
\\&&\le 
\int_{0}^{T} \Big(\frac12|\dot{w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^2_{t}+w^2(t))\Big)dt+2T \max|V_{\rm per}|.
\end{eqnarray*}

Hence, 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&
\mathbb E\Big(\int_0^{\widetilde \tau_2} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^2(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^2_t+ {\widetilde w}^2(t))\Big)dt\Big)
\\&&
\le 
2T (f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta) +4K\max V_{\rm per} + 2T\eta_K\max|V_{\rm per}|,
\end{eqnarray*}
recalling that $\lambda(r)<\eta/2$.

\bigskip 
We now prove by induction that for all $j\ge 2$, there exist $\widetilde w^{j}$, $\widetilde B^{j}_t$, and $\widetilde \tau^{j}$ with the following properties:

\smallskip
(i) $\widetilde w^{j}\in H^1((0,R);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for every $R>0$, $w^{j}(t)$ is $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j}_t$-measurable  for every $t>0$, 
 \begin{equation}\label{ii2}
 \widetilde w^j(t)=\widetilde w^j(  j T+(j-1)K) \hbox{ for } t\ge j T+(j-1)K,
 \end{equation}
and
 \begin{equation}\label{312}
 \widetilde w^j(jT+(j-1)K)=\sum_{\ell=1}^j(w^\ell(T)-  w^\ell(0)) +w^1(0);
 \end{equation}
 
\smallskip
(ii) $\widetilde B^{j}_t$ is Brownian motion adapted to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j}_t$;

\smallskip
(iii) $\widetilde \tau_{j}$ is a stopping time with respect to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j+1}_t$ such that 
 \begin{equation}\label{ii1}
jT+(j-1)K\le \widetilde \tau_{j}\le j T+ jK,
 \end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{r-j}
{\rm dist}\big(\widetilde B^{j}_{\tau_{j} } + \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde \tau_{j} ) - w^{j+1}(0) ,\mathbb Z^d\big)\le r
\end{equation}
except for a set $\Omega^{j}_K$ with $P(\Omega^{j}_K)< \eta_K$;

\smallskip
(iv) 
we have
\begin{eqnarray}\label{tre}\nonumber
&&\mathbb E\Big(\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j-1}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j}} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j}(t))\Big)dt\Big)
\\
&\le& 
T (f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta) +2K\max V_{\rm per} +2T\eta_K\max|V_{\rm per}|.
\end{eqnarray}

\medskip The construction above guarantees that these properties hold for $j=2$.
Suppose that we have constructed $\widetilde w^{j}$, $\widetilde B^{j}_t$ and $\widetilde \tau^{j}$ satisfying (i)--(iv) above.
We now define  $\widetilde w^{j+1}$, $\widetilde B^{j+1}_t$ and $\widetilde \tau^{j+1}$ satisfying (i)--(iv) above with $j+1$ in the place of $j$.

\smallskip
(i) For every $t>0$ we define $\widetilde w^{j+1}(t) $ as
$$
\widetilde w^{j+1}(t) =  \begin{cases}\widetilde w^{j}(t)  &\hbox{ for } 0\le t\le \widetilde \tau_{j} \\
\widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j} ) + w^{j+1}(t-\widetilde\tau_{j} ) -  w^{j+1}(0) 
&\hbox{ for }t> \widetilde \tau_{j} .\end{cases}
$$
We observe that $\widetilde w^{j+1}\in H^1((0,R);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for every $R>0$, and that for every $t>0$ the function $\omega\mapsto w^{j+1}(t) $ is $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j+1}_t$-measurable. Moreover, by \eqref{ii1} and \eqref{ii2},
 \begin{eqnarray*}
 \widetilde w^{j+1}((j+1)T+jK)&=& \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}((j+1)T+jK-\widetilde\tau_{j})-  w^{j+1}(0)
\\
&=&
\widetilde w^{j}(jT+(j-1)K)+ w^{j+1}(T)-  w^{j+1}(0)
\\
&=&
 \sum_{\ell=1}^j(w^\ell(T)-  w^\ell(0))+w^1(0) + w^{j+1}(T)-  w^{j+1}(0),
 \end{eqnarray*}
and claim (i) is proved.


\smallskip
(ii) We set
$$
\widetilde B^{j+1}_t = \begin{cases}\widetilde B^{j}_t  &\hbox{ for } 0\le t\le \widetilde \tau_{j} \\
 B^{j+1}_{t-\widetilde \tau_{j} } + \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j} }  &\hbox{ for }t> \widetilde \tau_{j} .\end{cases}
$$
By the strong Markov property this formula defines a Brownian motion on $[0,+\infty)$ adapted to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j+1}_t$.

\smallskip
(iii) We define the stopping time $\tau_{j+1} $ with respect to the filtration $\widetilde{\mathcal F}^{j+2}_t$  as the minimal $t\ge (j+1)T+jK$ such that
$$
{\rm dist}\big(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ \widetilde w^{j+1}(t)- w^{j+2}(0),\mathbb Z^d\big)\le r,
$$
or, equivalently, such that
$$
{\rm dist}\big(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ \widetilde w^{j+1}(\widetilde\tau_{j}+T)- w^{j+2}(0),\mathbb Z^d\big)\le r,
$$
recalling that $w^{j+1}(t)=w^{j+1}(T)$ for $t\ge T$.
Then, we set $$\widetilde\tau_{j+1} = \tau_{j+1} \wedge( (j+1)T+(j+1)K).$$ 
Note that, having set $\Omega^{j+1}_K=\{\widetilde\tau_{j+1}\neq\tau_{j+1}\}$, we still have $P(\Omega^{j+1}_K)<\eta_K$. 

\smallskip
(iv) We finally estimate
$$
\mathbb E\Big(\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j+1}} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt\Big).
$$
To that end, we note that
\begin{eqnarray*}\nonumber
&&\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j+1}} \Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt\\ \nonumber
&=&\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}\Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt\\
&&+\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}^{\widetilde \tau_{j+1}}\Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt,
\end{eqnarray*}
and that
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&
\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}\Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt
\\
&&=\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^j(t-\widetilde\tau_{j})|^2\\
&&\qquad +V_{\rm per}(
B^{j+1}_{t-\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}(t-\widetilde\tau_{j})-  w^{j+1}(0)\Big)dt
\\
&&
=\int_{0}^{T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(
B^{j+1}_{t}+ \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}(t)-  w^{j+1}(0)\Big)dt.
\end{eqnarray*}


On $\Omega\setminus \Omega^{j}_K$ by the inductive hypothesis (iii) we have
$$
\int_{0}^{T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(
B^{j+1}_{t}+ \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}(t)-  w^{j+1}(0)\Big)dt.
$$
$$
\le \int_{0}^{T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^{j+1}_{t}+  w^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt+\lambda(r)T,
$$
while on $\Omega^{j}_K$ we write 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\int_{0}^{T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(
B^{j+1}_{t}+ \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}(t)-  w^{j+1}(0)\Big)dt.
\\
&&
=\int_{0}^{T}\Big(\frac12|\dot w^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^{j+1}_{t}+  w^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt
\\&&
+\int_{0}^{T}\Big(V_{\rm per}(
B^{j+1}_{t}+ \widetilde B^{j}_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}+ \widetilde w^{j}(\widetilde\tau_{j})+ w^{j+1}(t)-  w^{j+1}(0)\Big)-V_{\rm per}(B^{j+1}_{t}+  w^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt.
\end{eqnarray*}
Hence, recalling that $\lambda(r)<\eta/2$,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{stima-1}\nonumber
&&\mathbb E\Big(\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}}^{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}\Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt\Big)\\
&
\le&  T (f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta) + T 2\eta_K \max|V_{\rm per}|.
\end{eqnarray}

Furthermore, we have 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{stima-2}\nonumber
\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}^{\widetilde \tau_{j+1}}\Big(\frac12|\dot{\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))\Big)dt
&=&\int_{\widetilde \tau_{j}+T}^{\widetilde \tau_{j+1}}V_{\rm per}(\widetilde B^{j+1}_t+ {\widetilde w}^{j+1}(t))dt
\\
& \le& 2 K\max|V_{\rm per}|.
\end{eqnarray}
From \eqref{stima-1} and \eqref{stima-2} we obtain claim (iv) with $j$ replaced by $j+1$.


\medskip

We finally define $\mathcal F^\xi_t=\widetilde{\mathcal F}^\infty_t$, $B^\xi_t$ and $w^\xi$ on $(0,+\infty)$ as 
\begin{equation}
B^\xi_t= \widetilde B^{j}_t,\qquad w^\xi(t)= \widetilde w^{j} (t)\hbox{ for } t\le jT.
\end{equation}
Since $\widetilde \tau_j\ge jT$ and  we have $\widetilde B^{j}_t= \widetilde B^k_t$ and $\widetilde w^{j}=\widetilde w^k$ on $[0,\widetilde \tau_j]$ for $k\ge j$, this is a good definition. We observe that $B^\xi_t$ is a Brownian motion adapted to the filtration $\mathcal F^\xi_t$, and   $w^\xi\in H^1((0,R);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for every $R>0$, and that for every $t>0$ the function $w^\xi(t)$ is $\mathcal F^\xi_t$-measurable. 
Eventually, \eqref{tre-b}  follows from \eqref{ii1} and \eqref{tre} by choosing $r$ small enough, and estimating
the integral on $(s_1,s_2)$ with the integral between $(\widetilde\tau_{j_1}, \widetilde\tau_{j_2})$, where 
$\widetilde\tau_{j_1}$ is the largest stopping time not greater than $s_1$ and 
$\widetilde\tau_{j_2}$ is the smallest stopping time not smaller than $s_2$.

body_md:

$$
jT+(j-1)K\le \widetilde \tau_{j}\le j T+ jK,
$$
and
$$
B^\xi_{\tau_{j} } + w^\xi(\widetilde \tau_{j} ) - w^{j+1}(0) \in \mathbb Z^d
$$
except for a set $\Omega^{j}_K$ with $P(\Omega^{j}_K)< \eta_K$, avoiding the error term $r$.
head: environment
name: correctors in the one-dimensional case

label: pro1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro1} 
There exists a constant $M>0$, independent of $K$ and $T$, such that 
$$
\mathbb E\Big(\int_a^b|\dot v_\varepsilon(t)|^2dt\Big)\le M (b-a)(|\xi|^2+1)
$$
for every $0\le a<b<+\infty$ and $0<\varepsilon<(b-a)/(3T+3K)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
With fixed  $0\le a<b<+\infty$, and  $0<\varepsilon<(b-a)/(3T+3K)$, let $j_a$ be the largest integer such that $\varepsilon (j_aT+(j_a-1)K)\le a$, and $j_b$ be the
 least integer such that $\varepsilon (j_bT+(j_b-1)K)\ge b$. 
  Then, after a change of variables, 
 we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb E\Big(\int_a^b|\dot v_\varepsilon(t)|^2dt\Big)&\le&\varepsilon
\mathbb E\,\bigg({\sum_{\ell=j_a}^{j_b-1}}\int_{\widetilde\tau_{\ell}}^{\widetilde\tau_{\ell}+T}|\dot w^\xi(t)|^2dt \bigg)
=\varepsilon
\mathbb E\bigg({\sum_{\ell=j_a}^{j_b-1}}\int_{0}^{T}|\dot w^\ell(t)|^2dt \bigg)\\
&
=&\varepsilon
(j_b-j_a)\mathbb E\,\bigg(\int_{0}^{T}|\dot w(t)|^2dt \bigg)\le\Big(\frac{b-a}{T+K}+2\varepsilon\Big)\mathbb E\Big(\int_{0}^{T}|\dot w(t)|^2dt\Big)\\
&\le& 
2\Big(\frac{b-a}{T+K}+2\varepsilon\Big)\Big(\int_{0}^{T}\mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per} (B_t+w(t))\Big)dt
+ T\max|V_{\rm per}|\Big)
\\
&\le& 
4(b-a) (|\xi|^2+\eta+ 2\max|V_{\rm per}|),
\end{eqnarray*}
using that $f_{\rm hom}(\xi)\le \frac12 |\xi|^2+\max|V_{\rm per}|$ and that $\varepsilon\le (b-a)/(3T+3K)$.
The claim is obtained by sending $\eta$ to $0$, and choosing e.g.~$M=4(1+2\max|V_{\rm per}|)$.
head: environment

label: pro2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro2} Let $0\le a<b<+\infty$.
For all sequences $\varepsilon_k\to 0$, the sequence $v_{\varepsilon_k}$ in \eqref{veh} converges in $(a,b)$ in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defco}} to the function given by $v_{\xi,T,K}$ given by 
$$
v_{\xi,T,K}(t)= x+\frac{T}{T+K} t \xi.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\varepsilon\lfloor \frac{x}\varepsilon\rfloor$ converges to $x$ in $\mathbb R^d$, it suffices to consider the case $x=0$.
By Proposition \ref{pro1}, up to subsequences, we can suppose that $v_{\varepsilon_k}\rightharpoonup \widehat v$ weakly in $H^1((a,b);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$.
To conclude we have only to prove that $\mathbb E(\widehat v(t)) = v_{\xi,T,K}(t)$. 

We note that for all $j\in\mathbb N$, setting $t^k_j:=\varepsilon_k(jT+(j-1)K)$, by \eqref{312} we have
$$
v_{\varepsilon_k}( t^k_j) =\varepsilon_k w^1(0)+ \varepsilon_k\sum_{\ell=1}^j (w^\ell(T)-w^\ell(0)),
$$
so that,   since $w^\ell\in X_0^{\ell,T}(\xi)$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathbb E(v_{\varepsilon_k}( t^k_j))&=&\varepsilon_k\mathbb E(w^1(0))+ \varepsilon_k\sum_{\ell=1}^j\mathbb E (w^\ell(T)-w^\ell(0))
\\
&=&\varepsilon_k\mathbb E(w(0))+ \varepsilon_k j \mathbb E (w(T)-w(0))
\end{eqnarray*}
and, recalling that  $w\in X_0^T(\xi)$, we have 
$$
\mathbb E(v_{\varepsilon_k}( t^k_j))=\varepsilon_k\mathbb E(w^1(0))+ \varepsilon_kj T \xi=\varepsilon_k\mathbb E(w^1(0)) +v_{\xi,T,K}(t^k_j) +{\varepsilon_k\frac{K}{T+K}}.
$$
  Since for all $t\in(a,b)$ and for all $k$ there exists $t^k_j$ such that $|t-t^k_j|\le \varepsilon_k(T+K)$, by the equi-H\"older continuity of $t\mapsto \mathbb E(v_{\varepsilon_k}( t))$ {(see Proposition \ref{pro1})}  we have
$$
|\mathbb E(v_{\varepsilon_k}( t))- \mathbb E(v_{\varepsilon_k}( t^k_j))|\le \sqrt{M\varepsilon_k(T+K)(|\xi|^2+1)}
$$
We then obtain the claim as $k\to+\infty$.

body_md:

With fixed $0\le a<b$, we have

\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}F_\varepsilon(v_\varepsilon,\mathcal F^\varepsilon_t,B^\varepsilon_t;{(a,b)})\le 
(b-a)\Big(f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\eta+ \Big(2\frac{K}{T}+2\eta_K\Big)\max|V_{\rm per}|\Big).

head: environment
name: recovery sequence for an affine target function

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\eta=\delta/4$, and let $K$ be large enough so that $2\eta_K\max|V_{\rm per}|\le \delta/4$.
Let $T_j$ be a diverging sequence such that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&f_{\rm hom}(\xi)=\lim_{j\to+\infty} \frac1{T_j}\inf\bigg\{\int_0^{T_j} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12|\dot w(t)|^2+V_{\rm per}(B^j_t+ w(t))\Big)dt: w\in X_0^{T_j}(\xi),  B^j_t ,  \mathcal F_t \bigg\}.
\end{eqnarray*}

By Proposition \ref{pro2} for all fixed $j$, the sequence $v^j_{\varepsilon}$ defined therein with $T=T_j$ converges in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defco}} to the function given by $v_{\xi,T,K}$ given by 
$$
v^j_{\xi,K}(t)= x+ \frac{T_j}{T_j+K} t \xi .
$$
Moreover, letting $\mathcal F^{j,\varepsilon}_t$ and $B^{j,\varepsilon}$ be the corresponding scaled filtration and Brownian motion,
by Proposition \ref{pro3} we have 
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}F_\varepsilon(v^j_\varepsilon,\mathcal F^{j,\varepsilon}_t,B^{j,\varepsilon}_t; (a,b))\le \Big(f_{\rm hom}(\xi)+\frac\delta2+ 2\frac{K}{T_j}\max|V_{\rm per}|\Big)(b-a).
$$
The conclusion follows by letting $j\to+\infty$ and using a diagonal argument.
head: environment

label: pro5
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{pro5}
With fixed $0\le a<b$, and $v$ piecewise affine, there exists $v_\varepsilon$ converging to $v$ in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defco}}, filtrations $\mathcal F^\varepsilon_t$, and Brownian motions $B^\varepsilon_t$ such that
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}F_\varepsilon(v_\varepsilon,\mathcal F^\varepsilon_t,B^\varepsilon_t; (a,b))\le 
\int_a^b f_{\rm hom}(v'(t))dt.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We define $a=a_0<a_1<\dots < a_m=b$ and $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m$ such that $v'(t)=\xi_i$ in $(a_{i-1}, a_i)$. It is not restrictive to suppose that $\tfrac{a_{i}}\varepsilon>\tfrac{a_{i-1}}\varepsilon+K$ for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
Note that, up to a translation, it is not restrictive to suppose that $v(t)=\xi_1t$ in the first interval. 

With fixed $\eta>0$, $T_0$ and $K$ we define $T_i>T_0$ and the correctors $\mathcal F^{\xi_i}_t$, $B^{\xi_i}_t$ and $w^{\xi_i}$ as in Proposition \ref{correct} for $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. It is not restrictive to suppose that the filtrations  $\mathcal F^{\xi_i}_t$ are mutually independent. For all $j$ we define 
$$
\widehat{\mathcal F}^j_t=\sigma\Big(\bigcup_{i=1}^j\mathcal F^{\xi_i}_t\Big).
$$

With fixed $\varepsilon>0$ we define $w^\varepsilon$, $\mathcal F^{\varepsilon}_t$, and $B^{\varepsilon}_t$ by a finite induction argument.
With fixed $r>0$ let $\tau^\varepsilon_1$ be the stopping time with respect to $\widehat{\mathcal F}^2_t$ defined as the smallest $t\ge a_1/\varepsilon$ such that
$$
{\rm dist}(B^{\xi_1}_t+w^{\xi_1}(\tfrac{a_1}\varepsilon)-w^{\xi_2}(0),\mathbb Z^d)\le r
$$
and set $\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_1=\tau^\varepsilon_1\wedge(\tfrac{a_1}\varepsilon+K)$.
For $t\ge 0$ we set 
$$
w^\varepsilon_1(t)=w^{\xi_1}(t) \hbox{ and }B^{\varepsilon,1}_t=B^{\xi_1}_t.
$$


For $t\ge0$ we then let 
$$
w^\varepsilon_2(t)=w^{\xi_2}((t-\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_1)^+)-w^{\xi_2}(0)+w^{\varepsilon,1}(t\wedge\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_1), \hbox{ and }B^{\varepsilon,2}_t=B^{\xi_2}_{(t-\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_1)^+}+ B^{\varepsilon, 1}_{t\wedge\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_1}.
$$
and let
$\tau^\varepsilon_2$ be the stopping time  with respect to $\widehat{\mathcal F}^3_t$ defined as the smallest $t\ge a_2/\varepsilon$ such that
$$
{\rm dist}(B^{\varepsilon,2}_t+w^\varepsilon_2(\tfrac{a_2}\varepsilon)-w^{\xi_3}(0),\mathbb Z^d)\le r
$$
and set $\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_2=\tau^\varepsilon_2\wedge(\tfrac{a_2}\varepsilon+K)$

This construction can then be iterated, by setting
for $t\ge0$  
$$
w^\varepsilon_i(t)=w^{\xi_i}((t-\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_{i-1})^+)-w^{\xi_i}(0)+w^{\varepsilon,{i-1}}(t\wedge\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_{i-1})\hbox{ and }B^{\varepsilon,i}_t=B^{\xi_i}_{(t-\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_{i-1})^+}+ B^{\varepsilon, {i-1}}_{t\wedge\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_{i-1}}.
$$
and letting
$\tau^\varepsilon_i$ be the stopping time  with respect to $\widehat{\mathcal F}^{i+1}_t$ defined as the smallest $t\ge a_i/\varepsilon$ such that
$$
{\rm dist}(B^{\varepsilon,i}_t+w^\varepsilon_i(\tfrac{a_2}\varepsilon)-w^{\xi_{i+1}}(0),\mathbb Z^d)\le r
$$
and set $\widetilde\tau^\varepsilon_i=\tau^\varepsilon_i\wedge(\tfrac{a_i}\varepsilon+K)$.
We finally set 
$$
w^\varepsilon(t):=w^\varepsilon_m(t), \ \ B^{\varepsilon}_t=B^{\varepsilon,m}_t,\ \hbox{ and }\mathcal F^\varepsilon_t=\widehat{\mathcal F}^{i+1}_t.
$$

If we consider $v_\varepsilon(t)= \varepsilon w^\varepsilon(t/\varepsilon)$, then $v_\varepsilon\to v_{K,\{T_i\}}$, the piecewise affine function with
$$
v'_{K,\{T_i\}}=  \frac{T_i}{T_i+K}\xi_i 
$$
on $(a_{i-1}, a_i)$.  After a diagonalization, the same computation as in Proposition \ref{pro3} gives the conclusion.

label: coro5
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{coro5}
The function $f_{\rm hom}\colon \mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is convex.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
With fixed $\xi_1$, $\xi_2\in  \mathbb R^d$, $\lambda\in(0,1)$, for all $k\in\mathbb N$ we consider the piecewise-affine function $u_k\colon (0,1)\to \mathbb R^d$, with $u_k(0)=0$ and whose derivative is the $\frac1k$-periodic function equal to $\xi_1$ on $(0,\lambda/k)$ and $\xi_2$ on $(\lambda/k,1/k)$. By Proposition \ref{pro5} for all $k\in\mathbb N$ there exists $u_{k,\varepsilon}$ converging to $u_k$ in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defco}}, filtrations $\mathcal F^{k,\varepsilon}_t$, and Brownian motions $B^{k,\varepsilon}_t$ such that
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\to 0}F_\varepsilon(u_{k,\varepsilon},\mathcal F^{k,\varepsilon}_t,B^{k,\varepsilon}_t; (0,1))\le \lambda f_{\rm hom}(\xi_1)+(1-\lambda) f_{\rm hom} (\xi_2).
$$
Note that the right-hand side is independent of $k\in\mathbb N$.
Since $u_k$ converge weakly in $H^1((0,1);\mathbb R^d)$ to to the function $u(t)=\xi t$, with $\xi=  \lambda  \xi_1+(1-\lambda) \xi_2$,  by a diagonal argument we can select a sequence $\varepsilon_k\to0$ such that the corresponding $u_{k,\varepsilon_k}$ converge to $u$ in the sense of Definition \ref{defco}, and 
$$
\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F_\varepsilon(u_{k,\varepsilon_k},\mathcal F^{k,\varepsilon_k}_t,B^{k,\varepsilon_k}_t; (0,1))\le \lambda f_{\rm hom}(\xi_1)+(1-\lambda) f_{\rm hom} (\xi_2).
$$
Since by Theorem \ref{main}(i) we have
$$
\liminf_{k\to+\infty}F_\varepsilon(u_{k,\varepsilon_k},\mathcal F^{k,\varepsilon_k}_t,B^{k,\varepsilon_k}_t; (0,1))\ge f_{\rm hom}(\xi)
$$
we conclude that $ f_{\rm hom}(\xi)\le \lambda f_{\rm hom}(\xi_1)+(1-\lambda) f_{\rm hom} (\xi_2)$; that is, the claim.

label: main-defect
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main-defect} Let $\widetilde F_\varepsilon$ be given by \eqref{deffe-dif}. Given $\varepsilon_k\to 0$, we have

\smallskip
{\rm(i)} For every $v\in H^1(a,b)$ and for every sequences $\mathcal F^k_t$,  $B^k_t$, and $v_k\to v$ such that 
$v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable, we have 
$$
F_{\rm hom} (v)\le\liminf_{k\to+\infty}\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t);
$$

\smallskip
{\rm(ii)} for every $v\in H^1(a,b)$ there exists sequences  $\mathcal F^k_t$,  $B^k_t$, and $v_k\to v$, such that 
$v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable,  such that
$$
F_{\rm hom} (v)\ge\limsup_{k\to+\infty}
\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t).
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $V_0\ge 0$ (i) follows from the analogous property in Theorem \ref{main}.

On order to prove (ii), we fix $\varepsilon_k$, $v_k$, $B^k_t$ and $\mathcal F^k_t$ with $v_k$ converging to some $v$. For every $s\ge 0$, let $\mu^k_s$ be the probability law of $ 
(\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}B^k_{t}+v_k(s))/\varepsilon_k$;
that is, for every Borel set $A$ in $\mathbb R$ 
$$
\mu^k_t(A):= P\Big(\Big\{\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}B^k_{t}+v_k(s)}{\varepsilon_k}\in A\Big\}\Big).
$$
We also introduce the probability measure defined by
$$
\mu^k(A):= \frac{1}{b-a}\int_{a}^{b}\mu^k_t(A)dt.
$$


We now fix {\color{red} $\eta>0$}, and $M\in\mathbb N$ such that $M^{-d}\le\eta$. Since $\mu^k([-ML,ML]^d)\le 1$, 
there exists $z_k\in\mathbb Z^d\cap[-ML,ML]^d$ such that
$$
\mu^k(z_k+[-L,L]^d)\le \frac1{M^d}\le\eta.
$$
We can then use as recovery sequence the same $B^k_t$ and $\mathcal F^k_t$, and the function $\widetilde v_k(t)= v_k(t)-\varepsilon_k z_k$, obtained by translating the function $v_k$. We note that $\widetilde v_k$ still converges to $v$ as $k\to +\infty$ since $z_k$ is bounded, and that 
$$
V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}-z_k\Big)=V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}\varepsilon\Big)
$$
by the periodicity of $V_{\rm per} $. Hence,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_k}(\widetilde v_k,\mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)=  F_{\varepsilon_k}(\widetilde v_k,\mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)+\int_a^{b} \mathbb E\Big(V_0 \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}-z_k\Big)\Big)dt
\end{eqnarray*}  
We now observe that
\begin{eqnarray*}
\int_a^{b} \mathbb E\Big(V_0 \Big(\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon_k} B^k_t+ v_k(t)}{\varepsilon_k}-z_k\Big)\Big)dt
\le (b-a)\eta \sup V_0.
\end{eqnarray*}  
Hence, we have
$$
F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)+ (b-a)\eta \sup V_0
\ge \widetilde F_{\varepsilon_k}(\widetilde v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t),
$$
which proves (ii) by choosing as $v_k$ as in the corresponding claim in Theorem \ref{main} {by the arbitrariness of $\eta$}.
head: environment

label: Hlambda
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{Hlambda}
Let  $\lambda>0$ be a given parameter. The space
$H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$ 
is defined as the space of
of all functions $u\colon(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb R^d$
 such that  $u\in H^1((0,t_0);\mathbb R^d)$ for all $t_0>0$,
and 
$$
\int_0^{+\infty} |u'(t)|^2  e^{-\lambda t}dt<+\infty,$$
endowed with the norm
$$
\Big(|u(0)|^2 +\int_0^{+\infty} |u'(t)|^2  e^{-\lambda t}dt\Big)^{1/2}.
$$
Similarly, the space
$H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ is defined as the space of
of all functions $u\colon(0,+\infty)\to L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$,
 such that $u\in H^1((0,t_0);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ for all $t_0>0$,
and 
$$
 \int_0^{+\infty} \mathbb E(|u'(t)|^2)  e^{-\lambda t}dt<+\infty,
$$
endowed with the norm
$$
\Big(\mathbb E (|u(0)|^2) +\int_0^{+\infty} \mathbb E(|u'(t)|^2)  e^{-\lambda t}dt\Big)^{1/2}.
$$
We observe that $H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$ and $H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ are {Hilbert} spaces.
head: environment

label: defcoinfty
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defcoinfty}
Let $\lambda>0$ be fixed. Given a sequence $v_k\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ and $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$ we write $v_k\to v$ if 
for all subsequences $v_{k_j}$, there exist a subsequence, that we still denote by $v_{k_j}$, 
and $\widehat v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$, possibly depending on the subsequence, such that 
$$
 v_{k_j}\rightharpoonup \widehat v \hbox{ weakly in }H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))
\quad\hbox{ and }\quad
\mathbb E(\widehat v(t))=v(t)\hbox{ for every }t.
$$

label: main2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main2} Given $\lambda>0$, let $F^\lambda_\varepsilon$ and $F_{\rm hom}^\lambda$ be given by \eqref{Fle} and \eqref{Flom}, respectively. Given $\varepsilon_k\to 0$, for every $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$ we have

\smallskip
{\rm(i)}  for every sequence of functions $v_k\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ with  $v_k\to v$ in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defcoinfty}},   for every sequence $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of filtrations such that each $v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable, and  for every sequence $\{B^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of Brownian motions adapted to $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$,
we have 
$$
F^\lambda_{\rm hom} (v)\le\liminf_{k\to+\infty}F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t);
$$

\smallskip
{\rm(ii)} there exist a sequence of functions $v_k\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ with  $v_k\to v$ in the sense of Definition {\rm\ref{defcoinfty}},  a sequence $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of filtrations such that each $v_k(t)$ is $\mathcal F^k_t$-measurable, and a sequence $\{B^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of Brownian motions adapted to $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$, such that 
$$
F^\lambda_{\rm hom} (v)\ge\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t).
$$
head: environment

label: deffeab
title: Proof
body_md:
Claim (i). Let $\{a_j\}_{j\ge0}$ be an increasing sequence in $[0,+\infty)$ with $a_0=0$ and $a_j\to+\infty$ as $j\to+\infty$. Using the notation
\begin{equation}\label{deffeab}
F_\varepsilon(v,\mathcal F_t,B_t; (a,b))= \int_a^{b} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt\varepsilon B_t+ v(t)}\varepsilon\Big)\Big)dt
\end{equation}
and Theorem \ref{main}, we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\liminf_{k\to+\infty}F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)
\ge \sum_{j\ge 1}\liminf_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t;(a_{j-1},a_j)) e^{-\lambda a_j}\\
\ge \sum_{j\ge 1}\int_{a_{j-1}}^{a_j}f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t)) e^{-\lambda a_j}dt
\
\ge \sum_{j\ge 1}e^{-\lambda(a_j-a_{j-1})}\int_{a_{j-1}}^{a_j}f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t)) e^{-\lambda t}dt\\
\ge \sup_{j\ge1}e^{-\lambda(a_j-a_{j-1})}\int_{0}^{+\infty}f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t)) e^{-\lambda t}dt.
\end{eqnarray*}
Since $\sup_{j\ge1}e^{-\lambda(a_j-a_{j-1})}$ can be taken arbitrarily close to $1$, we have proved the claim.

\medskip
Claim (ii).  By a density argument (see Proposition 4.5 in \cite{MR5057984}), it is sufficient to consider  a target function $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$ such that there exists $t_0$ such that $v(t)=0$ if $t\ge t_0$. We fix $t_1>t_0$. By Theorem \ref{main} with $(a,b)=(0,t_1)$, there exist $v_k$, $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}$, $\{B^k_t\}$ as in Claim (ii) of that theorem. By Lemma \ref{lemmada} we can assume that $\mathbb E(v_k(0))=v(0)$ and $\mathbb E(v_k(t_1))=v(t_1)=0$. The function $v_k$ is then extended by setting $v_k(t)=v_k(t_1)$ for $t\ge t_1$, and, recalling Definition \ref{Hlambda}, we have that $v_k\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega))$, and $v_k\to v$ in the sense of  Definition {\rm\ref{defcoinfty}}. Let $N\in\mathbb N$, and set $a_j=jt_1/N$. We note that, using the validity of Claim (i) of Theorem \ref{main} for $(a,b)=(a_{j-1}, a_j)$,  and the validity of Claim (ii) of the same theorem with $(a,b)=(0, t_1)$ we can prove $v_k$ satisfies Claim (ii) of Theorem \ref{main} with $(a,b)=(a_{j-1}, a_j)$ for any $j\in\{1,\ldots, N\}$. We then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)
\\
&\le& \sum_{j= 1}^N\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t;(a_{j-1},a_j)) e^{-\lambda a_{j-1}}
+\int_{t_1}^{+\infty} e^{-\lambda t}\max|V_{\rm per}|dt
\\
&\le& \sum_{j=1}^N\int_{a_{j-1}}^{a_j}f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t)) e^{-\lambda a_{j-1}}dt +e^{-\lambda t_1}\frac{\max|V_{\rm per}|}\lambda
\\
&\le& e^{t_1/N} \int_{0}^{t_1}f_{\rm hom} (\dot v(t)) e^{-\lambda t}dt+e^{-\lambda t_1}\frac{\max|V_{\rm per}|}\lambda.
\end{eqnarray*}
By the arbitrariness of $N$ and $t_1>t_0$ we conclude the proof.

title: Theorem
body_md: Given $\lambda$ and $x$ we have $U_\varepsilon(x)\to U_{\rm hom}(x)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.
head: environment

label: lifi
title: Proof
body_md:
With fixed $\varepsilon_k$ converging to $0$, we choose all $v_k\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$, with $\mathbb E(v_k(0))=x$, $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ filtrations such that $v(t)$ is measurable with respect to $\mathcal F^k_t$ for every $t$, and  $\{B^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ Brownian motions adapted to $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ such that 
$$
F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k,\mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)\le U_{\varepsilon_k}(x)+\frac1k .
$$
Using the constant function $x$ as competitor in \eqref{Uex}, from \eqref{Fle} we obtain that $U_{\varepsilon_k}(x)$ is bounded uniformly. Again, using \eqref{Fle} we then obtain
$$
\int_0^{+\infty} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v_k|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt\varepsilon B^k_t+ v_k}\varepsilon\Big)\Big)\, e^{-\lambda t}dt\le C,
$$
from which we deduce that $v_k$ is bounded in $H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$, and hence we can suppose that it converges to a function $\widehat v$ weakly in  $H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$. This implies that $v_k\to v$ in the sense of  Definition {\rm\ref{defcoinfty}}, where $v(t):= \mathbb E(\widehat v(t))$ for every $t\ge 0$, and $v(0)=\mathbb E(\widehat v(0))=x$. From Theorem \ref{main2}(i) we have that 
\begin{equation}\label{lifi}
U_{\rm hom}(x)\le  F^\lambda_{\rm hom}(v)\le \liminf_{k\to+\infty} F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k,\mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)\le \liminf_{k\to+\infty} U_{\varepsilon_k}(x).
\end{equation}

To prove 
\begin{equation}\label{lisu}
U_{\rm hom}(x)\ge \limsup_{k\to+\infty} U_{\varepsilon_k}(x),
\end{equation}
with fixed $\eta>0$ we consider  $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$, with $v(0)=x$, such that
$$
U_{\rm hom}(x)+\eta \ge F^\lambda_{\rm hom}(v).
$$
Let $v_k$, $\{\mathcal F^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$, and $\{B^k_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ be as in Theorem \ref{main2}(ii).
By Lemma \ref{lemmada} we can suppose that $\mathbb E(v_k(0))=x$ for every $k$. Thus we have
$$
U_{\rm hom}(x)+\eta\ge F^\lambda_{\rm hom}(v) \ge\limsup_{k\to+\infty}F^\lambda_{\varepsilon_k}(v_k, \mathcal F^k_t,B^k_t)\ge \limsup_{k\to+\infty}U_{\varepsilon_k}(x).
$$
By the arbitrariness of $\eta>0$ we get \eqref{lisu}, which, together with \eqref{lifi}, proves the claim.

label: Fle2
title: Remark
body_md:
\rm
For  $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ and $g\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d)$, we set
\begin{equation}\label{Fle2}
G^\lambda(v)= \int_0^{+\infty} \mathbb E(
\langle g(t),\dot v(t)\rangle)\, e^{-\lambda t}dt.
\end{equation}
We note that if $v_k\to v$ then
$$
\lim_{k\to+\infty}G^\lambda(v)= \int_0^{+\infty} 
\langle g(t),\dot v(t)\rangle\, e^{-\lambda t}dt.
$$


Indeed, if $v_k\rightharpoonup \widehat v$ in $H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$ then $v_k\rightharpoonup \widehat v$ in $L^2_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$, so that  $G^\lambda(v_k)\to G^\lambda(\widehat v)$, from which we conclude since
$$
G^\lambda(\widehat v)=\int_0^{+\infty} 
\langle g(t),\dot v(t)\rangle\, e^{-\lambda t}dt.
$$

Given $\lambda>0$,  define
\begin{equation}\label{73}
U_\varepsilon(x)=\inf_{\mathcal F_t,  B_t}\big\{ F^\lambda_\varepsilon(v,\mathcal F_t,B_t) + G^\lambda (v):  \mathbb E(v(0))=x\big\},
\end{equation}
where the infimum is taken over all $v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d))$,  such that $v(t)$ is measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_t$ for every $t$ and satisfies the initial condition, as well as over all  filtrations $\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ of $\mathcal F$ and  over all  Brownian motions $\{B_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ adapted to $\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\ge 0}$.
Similarly, we define
\begin{equation}\label{74}
U_{\rm hom}(x)=\inf\big\{ F^\lambda_{\rm hom}(v) +G^
\lambda(v): v\in H^1_\lambda((0,+\infty);\mathbb R^d), v(0)=x\big\}.
\end{equation}
We then have $U_\varepsilon(x)\to U_{\rm hom} (x)$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\rm From the arguments in Section \ref{defects}, we can conclude that, if $V_0$ is as in that section
and for any fixed uniformly continuous and bounded $\psi$, we also have that the value functions
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&U^0_{\varepsilon}(x)=\inf\Big\{
\int_0^{+\infty} \mathbb E\Big(\frac12 |\dot v(t)|^2+ V_{\rm per} \Big(\frac{\sqrt\varepsilon B_t+ v(t)}\varepsilon\Big)\\
&&
\hskip3cm+ V_0\Big(\frac{\sqrt\varepsilon B_t+ v(t)}\varepsilon\Big)+\psi(\sqrt\varepsilon B_t+ v(t))\Big)\, e^{-\lambda t}dt:  v(0)=x\Big\}
\end{eqnarray*}
converge to the value function $U_{\rm hom}$ for the unperturbed case in \eqref{Uom}.

Indeed, for a fixed sequence $\varepsilon_k$, we can apply the arguments in the proof of Theorem \ref{main-defect} to a sequence of almost minimizers $v_k$, $B^k$ for $U^0_{\varepsilon_k}$, upon defining $\mu^k$ as
$$
\mu^k(A):= \frac{1}{\lambda}\int_{0}^{+\infty}\mu^k_t(A)e^{-\lambda t}dt.
$$

This gives a variational proof of a convergence result for $U^0_\varepsilon$ by P.L.~Lions \cite{PLL-college}.
